learning_objectives: Explain line symmetry using simple language and an example.
Explain reflection using simple language and an example.
Explain symmetrical figures using simple language and an example.
Explain design patterns using simple language and an example.
Apply the chapter ideas independently in an unfamiliar but age-appropriate situation.

concept_map.mastery_evidence: Learner explains and applies line symmetry.
Learner explains and applies symmetrical figures.

lessons.objective: Learner can understand, explain and apply line symmetry.
teaching_sequence: Begin with a concrete or familiar situation.
Name the mathematical idea and connect it to prior knowledge.
Model a complete worked example with every step explained.
Move from representation to symbols and then to a new problem.
Ask the learner to explain the method without copying.
lessons.checkpoint: Explain line symmetry without notes and solve a new example.

items.question: Which approach best helps you understand line symmetry?
options: Identify what is known, represent it clearly, choose a valid method, and check the result.
Choose an operation before reading the problem.
Copy a worked answer.
Guess and stop.
items.explanation: Understanding the situation, choosing a method and checking the result makes mathematical reasoning reliable.

items.question: Explain line symmetry as if you were teaching it to someone learning from the basics.
items.answer: A correct response defines line symmetry, gives a simple example, and explains the reasoning.

items.question: Create and solve a new everyday problem involving line symmetry.
items.expected_response: A valid problem, correct solution and explanation of the method.

options: Use major ideas independently in a new situation and explain the reasoning.
Finish the lesson without checking understanding.

flashcards.back: Define line symmetry, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define reflection, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define symmetrical figures, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define design patterns, give an example, and explain why it matters.

interactive_activities.title: Explore line symmetry
interactive_activities.instructions: Use a safe, age-appropriate task specifically focused on line symmetry. Record what you notice, explain it, and state what you learned.

interactive_activities.title: Use it in a new situation
interactive_activities.instructions: Create a new situation where reflection is useful and explain your reasoning.

interactive_activities.title: Teach it back
interactive_activities.instructions: Teach design patterns to a beginner in 3–5 clear steps.
